citations.label: Paper, AI Assistance Reduces Persistence and Hurts Independent Performance
citations.excerpt: Here, through a series of randomized controlled trials on human-AI interactions (N = 1,222), we provide causal evidence for two key consequences of AI assistance: reduced persistence and impairment of unassisted performance.

citations.label: Paper, AI Assistance Reduces Persistence and Hurts Independent Performance
citations.excerpt: Across a variety of tasks, including mathematical reasoning and reading comprehension, we find that although AI assistance improves performance in the short-term, people perform significantly worse without AI and are more likely to give up. Notably, these effects emerge after only brief interactions with AI (approximately 10 minutes).

citations.label: Knowledge at Wharton, Without Guardrails, Generative AI Can Harm Education, study design
citations.excerpt: A new study led by researchers at Wharton and Penn reveals that using generative AI improves student performance, but also makes it harder for students to learn and acquire new skills. The researchers designed an experiment with nearly 1,000 high school math students in Turkey to determine whether large language models can harm or help their education.
